items.title: Fell Asleep in the Sun
items.summary: The Los Angeles band’s note-perfect reverence for 2000s trip-hop, soft rock, and breakbeat pop makes for a superficially pretty but frustratingly shallow debut LP.

items.title: I Lost My Way for Centuries
items.summary: On a sprawling yet accessible double album that trades murky electronics for mostly analog instruments, Dylan McCartney and co. inject record-collector touchstones with a contemporary sense of unease.

items.title: The Meaning of Flowers
items.summary: Dominated by exquisite vocal melodies and an abiding sense of mystery, the Danish musician’s new album is simultaneously otherworldly and profoundly earthy.

items.title: SUAHN, “Distort Everything Forever”
items.summary: The Baltimore post-hardcore guitarist galvanizes personal struggles into stark, unsettling club jams. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: A Journey Through Ghetto House and Juke
items.summary: How a crew of South and West Side producers transformed house music—and laid the groundwork for footwork. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Ride Lonesome
items.summary: The blues sound a little gray on Beck’s new album, a spiritual sequel to Morning Phase blending country-folk songwriting and gently psychedelic West Coast rock.

items.title: Age of the Exhibitionist
items.summary: The pop singer’s second album constructs a voyeuristic fantasy out of durable, club-friendly dance-pop with enough eccentricities to keep things interesting.

items.title: Scour Order
items.summary: Amid a career of ceaseless experimentation, the New York black metal band finally gives into nostalgia. They’re having a blast just letting it rip.

items.title: These Killing Times
items.summary: Casting a wide collaborative net across the world of heavy music, the Portland musician captures a newfound sense of momentum, even optimism, in her doomy, downcast songwriting.

items.title: Easy Rider (Music From the Soundtrack)
items.summary: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the blockbuster soundtrack for the 1969 biker classic: a generational bounty of radio hits that, taken together, sounds like a dying dream.

items.title: Second Song
items.summary: The 80-year-old musician’s 50th studio album emphasizes atmosphere over songcraft, but its long, rambling tracks offer ample reminders of his melodic dexterity and lyrical gifts.

items.title: A Brief History of Atlantic Canada’s Guitar Pop Explosions
items.summary: Canada’s four Atlantic provinces punch above their weight when it comes to producing guitar pop. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Laurentius the Profit Found Heaven in a Cave
items.summary: The Berlin artist traveled to a cave church in Turkey to record an album where mistakes, echoes, and rough edges are essential to the story. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Curly Castro, “Yaphet”
items.summary: Curly Castro draws on the sound of pulpy, Blaxpoitation cinema for his latest batch of songs. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Day and Night
items.summary: Carly Rae Jepsen’s sprawling new double album celebrates full-time love and commitment with sweet, sunny tracks for Day and sleeker, dancier songs for Night.

items.title: Pylon
items.summary: Members of Turnstile, Deftones, Paramore, and Pinegrove push Bea Kristi toward slightly grungier, angstier territory on her fourth album.

items.title: Angel
items.summary: After going viral with swooning, rom-com-ready songs, the singer-songwriter takes a more homespun approach on her fourth album, a set of folk-influenced tracks buoyed by a wandering spirit.

items.title: Secret to Spare
items.summary: On its debut album, the refreshingly sincere L.A. power-pop quartet wears its heart—and its influences—on its sleeve.

items.title: lucy miró al mundo y notó que está girando
items.summary: With an assist from Jane Remover and under the influence of the Beatles, the rising Chilean star crafts a digirock ode to emotional overload.

items.title: Wet
items.summary: Steamy and subversive, the new album from former LCD Soundsystem collaborator Gavilán Rayna Russom’s long-running project is a queer electro manifesto.

items.title: Put Rings on All My Fingers to Weigh Down My Hands EP
items.summary: The London band’s mesmeric debut EP suffuses noise and drone in pastoral loveliness—or is it the other way around?

items.title: Hope Is the Thing With Feathers
items.summary: Focused on community and resilience, the folk singer and multi-instrumentalist’s new album anchors her wide-ranging musical explorations in her Carolina roots.
